title: Atrial fibrillation
summary: Atrial fibrillation stops, sinus rhythm returns for a while, and then the atria fibrillate again.
description: In atrial fibrillation the atria do not contract together: there are no P waves, the baseline wavers, and the ventricles beat at irregular intervals. In this excerpt the fibrillation stops after about 20 seconds; after a pause of a couple of seconds, sinus rhythm returns, with a P wave before each QRS, and then the atria start to fibrillate again. The strip at the top names the rhythm, as the cardiologists who labelled it did.
look_for: No P waves, and irregular R–R intervals, during the fibrillation
The pause when the fibrillation stops
A P wave before each QRS in sinus rhythm, and the more regular R–R intervals

channels.name: ECG (V1)

events.title: A P wave that was not conducted to the ventricles (a missed beat)
